hooks.text: An explosion shone twenty times brighter than our entire Milky Way galaxy.
A single cosmic flash reached a peak brightness 570 billion times greater than the Sun.
Automated telescopes in Chile spotted a cosmic explosion that defied the laws of physics.

title: The Cosmic Explosion Brighter Than Twenty Galaxies
description: Discover ASASSN-15lh, a mysterious cosmic explosion that outshined the Milky Way twenty times over and radiates more energy than the Sun's entire lifetime.

beats.text: An explosion shone twenty times brighter than our entire Milky Way galaxy.
beats.visual: Artist concept of a superluminous supernova explosion, 2015

beats.text: In June 2015, twin automated telescopes located in Chile discovered ASASSN-15lh blazing brilliantly across the dark night sky.
beats.visual: Cerro Tololo Inter American Observatory telescope dome in Chile, 2015
subjects: All Sky Automated Survey for SuperNovae
queries: Cerro Tololo Inter American Observatory buildings

beats.text: The incredible event reached a peak brightness 570 billion times greater than our Sun.
beats.visual: Supernova remnant artist concept in deep space, 2015

beats.text: Located roughly 3.8 billion light-years away, its strange spectrum completely lacked hydrogen and helium lines.
beats.visual: South African Large Telescope dome at Sutherland, 2015

beats.text: Unlike typical blasts in small dwarf galaxies, this mysterious explosion erupted inside a massive galaxy.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope view of a massive distant galaxy, 2015

beats.text: Astronomers actively debate whether it was powered by a fast-spinning magnetar or a supermassive black hole.
